findings.finding: AC8 says the hook denies "any unterminated heredoc", and the docs row in `docs/hooks-and-pipeline.md` repeats that unqualified ("or whose heredoc delimiter is never closed"). The implementation only denies unterminated heredocs whose opener line runs an interpreter (`pending.append((word, dash, runs_interpreter))` + the `interpreter` filter). An unterminated `cat <<'EOF'` passes. The narrowing was deliberate (per the code-review reply) but the spec text and docs row were not updated to match.
findings.suggestion: Either reword AC8 / the docs row to "an unterminated heredoc feeding an interpreter", or drop the `runs_interpreter` filter.

findings.finding: Heredoc delimiters outside `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]` are not recognized as heredocs. A well-formed command like `uv run python - <<'PY-SCRIPT' … PY-SCRIPT` (hyphen, digit-leading, or `$VAR` delimiters) never registers an opener, so the body is not masked and the closer line is not consumed — the opener line still matches `_stdin_python` and the command is falsely denied, violating AC8's "well-formed forms pass". A body line containing `; python -` after a failed opener recognition could conversely be falsely denied too.
findings.suggestion: Widen the delimiter group (e.g. `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_\-]` and optionally `\$?[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]`) and add allow/deny tests for hyphenated and variable delimiters.

findings.finding: python 2>/dev/null -` (redirect before the `-`) passes `_is_stdin_python`: the token `2>/dev/null` hits the "different command" bail-out before `-` is seen, yet stdin is still the terminal — exactly the hang AC8 targets. Also `python - 0<&-`-style forms after the `-` are fine, but this ordering variant is a concrete miss. The docstring says "first non-option argument is `-`", so it is at least self-consistent, but the guard's purpose (prevent stdin waits) is defeated for this shape.
findings.suggestion: After locating the interpreter, treat `<`/`>` redirection tokens as skippable rather than terminal when they appear before `-`.

findings.finding: Only the last six non-empty lines are examined. The auth error can scroll out of that window inside one 15 s poll (the agent often prints several lines after a failed call), after which the run waits out the full idle abort — the exact failure AC4 was written to eliminate. Terminal text is also wrapped by xterm; a line can be split so "Login expired" starts mid-line beyond the `.{0,6}` allowance (e.g. a timestamp prefix longer than 6 chars).
findings.suggestion: Search the last ~40 lines (or a bounded slice like the existing `terminal.slice(-2000)` used for the idle signature) rather than 6, and consider matching "Login expired" without the strict 6-char prefix bound.

findings.finding: The integration test parses the hooks.json command with `guard_cmd.split('"')[1]` — a command variant using single quotes or extra quoted args would break the test (or silently pick the wrong segment). It also never exercises the `uv run --no-project` prefix that production uses; the "runs the hook through its real hooks.json command line" claim in the Confidence Calibration is overstated.
findings.suggestion: Resolve the script path with a small regex for the quoted path, and optionally run one case through the full registered command line (with `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` substituted).

findings.finding: The new fallback host extraction applies to every `new URL` failure in `findExternalUse`, including the SCHEMELESS path (`hostOf("http://" + m[1])`). Strings that previously fell through as raw text (and were tested verbatim against `LOOPBACK`/`HARMLESS_HOSTS`) are now reduced to a leading token — e.g. a schemeless hit like `"api.example.com/foo bar baz"` now yields `api.example.com` either way, but odd inputs like `localhost:foo` where `new URL` throws now extract `localhost` and are exempted where previously the raw string `localhost:foo` may not have matched `LOOPBACK`. Net effect is probably only more exemptions (weaker S05), not false flags, but it is a behavior change on an existing path with no test covering the fallback's interaction with `HARMLESS_HOSTS`.
findings.suggestion: Add one test where the fallback path extracts a host that is harmless vs one that is not, to pin the semantics.

findings.finding: Masking quoted arguments removes their position entirely. A valid command such as `python "tools/check.py" -` becomes `python -` and is denied, although Python executes a script with `-` as its argument. This globally blocks legitimate Bash calls.
findings.suggestion: Preserve quoted arguments as opaque tokens rather than whitespace, so script paths remain positional arguments. Add an allow test for a quoted script path followed by `-`.

findings.finding: The heredoc matcher only recognizes identifier-shaped delimiters. For example, `python - <<'PY-END'\nprint(1)` passes despite its unterminated heredoc: no delimiter is recorded, and the remaining `<<` makes the bare-input check treat the command as fed. This leaves AC8 partially implemented.
findings.suggestion: Recognize shell heredoc words, including quoted delimiters containing punctuation or starting with digits. Test both terminated and unterminated forms.

findings.finding: Restricting detection to six lines still aborts on ordinary source output. A terminal tail containing `+ // authentication_failed handler` matches and stops the run even when authentication succeeded. The negative test only checks source text followed by eight unrelated lines, so it misses this case.
findings.suggestion: Match recognizable agent error records rather than these substrings anywhere in the tail. Add negative tests with matching source text inside the last six lines.  Overall assessment: ship-with-fixes. The harness and prompt changes largely satisfy the specification, but the global guard and auth detector need these concrete parsing fixes before shipping.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
